graders.name: overview-not-invented
graders.evidence:
# Overview

`acme-tool` is a small Node.js ESM package (`package.json:1`) with one declared entry
point: the `acme` binary bound to `src/cli/main.js:1`. The kit folds the source into
three components (rules in `fold-rules.json`, one component per top-level `src/*` dir):

| component | files | role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| cli | `src/cli/main.js` | entry point; imports `core` and `web`, then calls both unconditionally |
| core | `src/core/run.js`, `src/core/back.js` | `run()` returns the constant `1` (`src/core/run.js:1`) |
| web | `src/web/server.js` | `serve(app)` ignores `app` and calls `core.run()` (`src/web/server.js:1`) |

Full detail: `docs/reference/components.md`.

## What actually happens at runtime
`src/cli/main.js:1` runs unconditionally on invocation: `run(); serve(express);` — there
is no argument parsing (no `process.argv` handling, no CLI-arg library) and no branching,
so every invocation of `acme` takes the same path regardless of arguments.
`serve(express)` passes the `express` module itself (not an `express()` app instance) into
`web.serve`, which never calls `.listen()` anywhere in the repo. **No HTTP server is ever
started** — despite the `express` dependency and web-shaped classification signal, `web`
is inert code that only re-calls `core.run()`.

`src/core/back.js:1` re-exports `web.serve` as `back`; nothing in the repo imports `back`
(dead code).

## Cycle
`core` and `web` import each other (1 edge each way, `docs/reference/components.md`):
`src/core/back.js` → `src/web/server.js` → `src/core/run.js`. Whether to accept this by ADR or split
the components is an open decision — see `interview.md` Q2.

## Open classification question
Classification is ambiguous between `cli` and `service` (evidence: `package.json` `bin`
field, and the `express` dependency) — see `interview.md` Q1. Given the above (no server is
ever started), the `cli` reading is closer to what the code does today, but this is a human
call, not one this review makes unilaterally.
